questions.prompt: Which vitamin deficiency is seen in infants with jaundice who undergo phototherapy?
questions.explanation: B2 is the best answer. Phototherapy can degrade riboflavin, making vitamin B2 deficiency a recognized risk.

questions.prompt: Which of the following fatty acid has 16 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Palmitic acid is the best answer. Palmitic acid is the 16-carbon saturated fatty acid 16:0.

questions.prompt: Binding of the prokaryotic RNA polymerase to promoter site is inhibited by ........?
questions.explanation: Rifampicin is the best answer. RNA polymerase and its factors copy a DNA template into RNA. Rifampicin is the intended drug. More precisely, it binds the bacterial RNA-polymerase beta subunit and blocks early RNA-chain extension, rather than simply preventing promoter recognition.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following inactivates the 60S subunit of eukaryotic ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Ricin is the best answer. Ricin depurinates 28S rRNA in the eukaryotic 60S subunit and inactivates it. Ricin irreversibly depurinates 28S rRNA in the 60S subunit. Cycloheximide also inhibits eukaryotic elongation at the large subunit; the intended distinction is ricin-mediated ribosome damage.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following mediates carrying genetic information from DNA to protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: m-RNA is the best answer. mRNA carries coding information from DNA to ribosomes.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following vitamins is involved in the structure of coenzyme A?
questions.explanation: Pantothenate (B 5 ) is the best answer. Pantothenate, vitamin B5, is a structural component of coenzyme A.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following vitamins provides the coenzyme for γ-carboxylation reactions?
questions.explanation: Menaquinone is the best answer. Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K have distinct stored functions and deficiency patterns.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Okazaki fragments are formed during the synthesis of ..................?
questions.explanation: DNA is the best answer. Okazaki fragments are short DNA segments synthesized on the lagging strand.

questions.prompt: Where does a repressor bind to an operon?
questions.explanation: Operator is the best answer. Operators, repressors, activators, and feedback control gene expression.

questions.prompt: In vitamin B6 deficiency, which other vitamin deficiency may also be observed?
questions.explanation: B3 is the best answer. Water-soluble vitamins commonly serve as coenzyme precursors and have characteristic deficiency syndromes.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: A child with tall stature, loose joints, and detached retinas is found to have a mutation in type II collagen. Recall that collagen consists of a repeating tripeptide motif where the first amino acid of each tripeptide is the same. Which of the following amino acids is the recurring amino acid most likely to be altered in mutations that distort collagen molecules?
questions.explanation: Glycine is the best answer. Protein function follows primary sequence and higher-order folding interactions.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Lactose utilization by E. coli requires which lac gene products?
questions.explanation: LacY permease imports lactose and LacZ beta-galactosidase hydrolyzes it. Both A and B are valid for the unrestricted original question.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: The oxygen carrier of muscle is the globular protein myoglobin. Which one of the following amino acids is highly likely to be localized within the interior of the molecule?
questions.explanation: Valine is the best answer. Valine is nonpolar and is therefore favored in the hydrophobic interior of a globular protein.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about Michaelis-Menten constant is correct?

options.text: The Km of an enzyme is unchanged when the enzyme concentration is increased.
A low Km indicates a high affinity of an enzyme for its substrate.
A high Km indicates a high affinity of an enzyme for its substrate.
The Km of an enzyme increases when the enzyme concentration is increased.

questions.explanation: A low Km indicates a high affinity of an enzyme for its substrate. is the best answer. Michaelis-Menten parameters relate substrate concentration to reaction velocity. Km is independent of total enzyme concentration in the Michaelis-Menten model. Low Km is often used as an affinity shorthand, but Km is not universally a dissociation constant. The original wording permits both A and the customary textbook interpretation of B.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Actinomycin D is an inhibitor of ..................?
questions.explanation: Transcription is the best answer. RNA polymerase and its factors copy a DNA template into RNA.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: What is the starting compound for the synthesis of sphingolipids?
questions.explanation: Ceramide is the best answer. Ceramide is the structural core of sphingolipids. Ceramide is the common branch-point precursor for complex sphingolipids. De novo synthesis begins earlier with serine and palmitoyl-CoA; do not mistake the offered intermediate for the first substrates.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: In which reaction does biotin participate?
questions.explanation: Carboxylation is the best answer. Water-soluble vitamins commonly serve as coenzyme precursors and have characteristic deficiency syndromes.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which on of the following is the main form of vitamin D in plasma?
questions.explanation: 25-Hydroxycholecalciferol (25 (OH)-D3) is the best answer. Water-soluble vitamins commonly serve as coenzyme precursors and have characteristic deficiency syndromes.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: What is the main function of t-RNA?

options.text: Identifies amino acids and transports them to ribosomes

questions.explanation: Identifies amino acids and transports them to ribosomes is the best answer. Ribosomes read mRNA through tRNA-mediated amino-acid delivery.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following mechanisms will remove uracil and incorporate the correct base?
questions.explanation: Base excision repair is the best answer. DNA repair pathways recognize a lesion, remove it, resynthesize DNA, and seal the strand.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following enzymes is required for end to end joining of DNA?
questions.explanation: DNA ligase is the best answer. Replication requires directional synthesis, proofreading, and coordinated fork enzymes.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: What is the role of sigma factor in bacterial RNA polymerase?

options.text: Positioning RNA polymerase correctly on the DNA template

questions.explanation: Positioning RNA polymerase correctly on the DNA template is the best answer. Sigma positions bacterial RNA polymerase at the correct promoter.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: According to Chargaff’s rule, in a DNA molecule the percentage of ...............?
questions.explanation: T+G=A+C is the best answer. Because A=T and G=C in double-stranded DNA, T+G equals A+C.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following vitamins is directly involved in the conversion of homocysteine to methionine?
questions.explanation: B12 (Cobalamin) is the best answer. Vitamin B12 is the cofactor for methionine synthase.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which vitamin deficiency cause hemolytic anemia?
questions.explanation: E is the best answer. Vitamin E deficiency permits oxidative membrane damage and can cause hemolytic anemia.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about mRNA?

options.text: Cap is added to the 5′ end
Exons are removed and introns are spliced together
A poly-A tail is added to the 3′ end

questions.explanation: B and C are both incorrect. Replication-dependent histone mRNAs are capped but usually lack poly-A tails. Splicing removes introns and joins exons. Polyadenylation is typical, not universal.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: The highest concentration of cystine can be found in .............?
questions.explanation: Keratin is the best answer. Keratin is rich in cystine disulfide bonds, which strengthen hair and nails.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: The phenomenon of mutarotation is due to which of the following?

options.text: Conversion of linear Glucose to circular form

questions.explanation: Conversion of α-D-Glucose to β-D-Glucose is the best answer. Mutarotation is interconversion of α and β anomers through the open-chain form.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following phospholipids is the main component of inner mitochondrial membrane?
questions.explanation: Cardiolipin is the best answer. Cardiolipin is the signature phospholipid of the inner mitochondrial membrane. Cardiolipin is the characteristic, functionally important inner-mitochondrial phospholipid intended by the exam. It is not necessarily the most abundant phospholipid by mass; “main component” is imprecise.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about solutions of amino acids at physiologic pH is true?

options.text: Some amino acids contain only positive charges
All amino acids contain both positive and negative charges
All amino acids contain positively charged side chains
All amino acids contain negatively charged side chains

questions.explanation: All amino acids contain both positive and negative charges is the best answer. At physiological pH, free amino acids generally contain both NH3+ and COO- groups as zwitterions.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a deoxy sugar?
questions.explanation: L-Fucose is the best answer. L-Fucose is 6-deoxy-L-galactose.

questions.prompt: Galactonic acid is caused by oxidation of which factor in galactose?
questions.explanation: Aldehyde group is the best answer. Monosaccharide composition and glycosidic linkage define carbohydrate behavior. Oxidation of the aldehyde group gives the aldonic acid. An aldehyde contains a carbonyl group, so both the broad and specific choices describe that same site.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: The enzyme responsible for the removal of supercoiling in replicating DNA, ahead of the replication fork, is ................?
questions.explanation: Topoisomerase is the best answer. Topoisomerase relieves torsional stress ahead of the replication fork.
questions.subject: biochemistry

questions.prompt: Which enzyme class catalyzes the reaction shown?
questions.explanation: Glucose-6-phosphate and fructose-6-phosphate are aldose/ketose isomers. Phosphoglucose isomerase interconverts them without changing overall oxidation state.

questions.prompt: Which membrane fatty acids serve as precursors for eicosanoids?

options.text: C20 and C22 saturated fatty acids
C18 and C22 polyunsaturated fatty acids
C20 and C22 monounsaturated fatty acids
C20 and C22 polyunsaturated fatty acids

questions.explanation: Eicosanoids are generated from long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids released from membrane phospholipids; arachidonic acid is the major C20 precursor. This paper uses eicosanoid loosely for lipid mediators from C20/C22 PUFAs. Strictly, eicosanoids derive from C20 precursors; C22 DHA gives docosanoids. The offered D is the intended broad PUFA choice, not the precise definition.

questions.prompt: Which amino acid is involved in N-glycosidic bond formation?

questions.prompt: Which of the following would produce Methemoglobinemia?

questions.explanation: Converting Ferrous iron (Fe2+) to Ferric (Fe3+) is the best answer. Oxidation of heme iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+ forms methemoglobin, which cannot bind oxygen normally.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lipoproteins is produced via the exogenous lipoprotein pathway?

Hydrolysis of procollagen to form collagen

questions.prompt: Hydroxyapatite has a very small dissolution equilibrium constant (approximately 10^-26 in the source). Which description is correct under physiological conditions?

options.text: It is relatively insoluble under physiological conditions
It dissolves only in basic solutions
It would dissolve well in calcium phosphate solution
It dissolves well under physiological conditions

questions.explanation: A very small dissolution equilibrium constant favors solid hydroxyapatite. Acid promotes dissolution; added calcium/phosphate can suppress it by the common-ion effect. Source correction: hydroxyapatite is the inorganic mineral component of bone, not the organic matrix.
